gen_risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder engagement may lead to exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a strong, adequately budgeted, and operational Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) to track and respond to grievances from target populations

gen_risks.description: Financial management risks may lead to inaccurate or untimely information on project status
gen_risks.mitigation: Update existing financial management manuals, upgrade accounting software, and recruit an external auditor

gen_risks.description: Procurement risks may lead to delays, governance issues, or limited market competition
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire experienced procurement specialists, conduct early market engagement, and adopt flexible procurement approaches

gen_risks.description: Environmental risks may lead to community health risks, occupational health and safety risks, or nuisances related to air and noise emissions
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare an Umbrella Environmental and Social Management Framework (U-ESMF) and adapt it to country context
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV. D. Environmental and Social

gen_risks.description: Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) risks may lead to harm to beneficiaries or staff
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare country-specific Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and SEA risk assessments and develop corresponding SEA Action Plans
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV. D. Environmental and Social

gen_risks.description: Climate change may lead to increased health risks, particularly for vulnerable populations
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate change considerations into project design and implementation, including climate-resilient infrastructure and health services
gen_risks.evidence: Section C. Relevance to Higher Level Objectives

gen_risks.description: Fragility, conflict, and violence may lead to disruptions in health services or increased health risks
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop contingency plans and establish emergency response mechanisms to address potential disruptions

gen_risks.description: Inadequate health infrastructure may lead to reduced access to health services or increased health risks
gen_risks.mitigation: Invest in health infrastructure upgrades, including green and resilient solutions, to improve access to health services

gen_risks.description: Inadequate human resources for health may lead to reduced capacity to respond to health emergencies
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and implement human resources for health plans, including training and capacity-building programs

gen_risks.description: Inadequate laboratory capacity may lead to reduced ability to detect and respond to health emergencies
gen_risks.mitigation: Invest in laboratory upgrades, including equipment and training, to improve capacity for disease detection and response

gen_risks.description: Inadequate risk communication and community engagement may lead to reduced effectiveness of health emergency response
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and implement risk communication and community engagement strategies, including training and capacity-building programs

gen_risks.description: Inadequate gender considerations may lead to reduced effectiveness of health emergency response
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate gender considerations into project design and implementation, including training and capacity-building programs

gen_risks.description: Inadequate environmental and social considerations may lead to negative impacts on communities or the environment
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare and implement environmental and social management plans, including stakeholder engagement and monitoring
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV. D. Environmental and Social

gen_risks.description: Inadequate governance and institutional capacity may lead to reduced effectiveness of health emergency response
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and implement governance and institutional capacity-building programs, including training and capacity-building programs

gen_risks.description: Inadequate financial management and procurement may lead to reduced effectiveness of health emergency response
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and implement financial management and procurement plans, including training and capacity-building programs

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
